newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Nong Ngu Hao airport saga took a new twist yesterday when the Air Force refused to 'completely' move out of its present hedquarters to allow expansion of the Don Muang international airport.
This ruled out full-scale expansion of the Don Muang Airport and means the Nong Ngu Hao second airport project is unlikely to be scrapped or face a long delay, observers said. (The Nation)

- Deputy Prime Minister Montri Pongpanich came back with a vengeance in the Nong Ngu Hao row yeserday, claiming a certain individual was paid by a neighbouring country to satobage the second national airort project.
Montri neither named names nor produce any evidence to substantiate his claim, saying only that it was a rumour which had been around for a long time. (BANKGOK POST) + + + +

- United Communication Industry Plc (Ucom) will try its hand at the news business after winning a 20-year concession from the Public Relations Department to operate the PRD's network of 40 radio stations.
A radio industry source said Ucom had approached the Independent News Network (INN), a news service and radio news operator, wanting to take a share of that company (Bangkok Post)

- Confusion appears to have clouded the future of the new Bangkok international airport project at Nong Ngu Hao with the Chavalit government unable to announce a clear-cut policy on this important infrastructure scheme following suggestions to relocate the project or suspend it.

Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan yesterday asked for a one-month study of all issues concerned with the project. He also identified two potential options for the government -- expand the exisiting airport while waiting completion of Nong Ngu Hao or expand the exisiting airport without building the second airport at all. (The Nation)
